title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-08-18
lineage: AUD mC > Rx2 > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality audience tape of a historic 8/18/70 show with debut performances (Ripple, Brokedown Palace, Operator, Truckin') and a stellar acoustic set.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience capture that is lo‑fi and a bit boomy, but surprisingly listenable for 1970. Musically the concert shines – the acoustic half is praised as “fantastic,” and the electric set delivers several first‑time debuts and strong renditions of The Other One, Attics, Man’s World and more.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rave about the historic setlist and performances (≈4.5/5 show rating) while noting only modest technical flaws in the audience recording (≈3/5). Weighted average yields ~4.1 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pocket‑recorder lo‑fi tape; noticeable boominess around 960 Hz, occasional muffled passages and background noises (goats/sheep), but overall listenable after a brief adjustment period.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic set is highlighted as superb and very well‑executed; electric set, while not uniformly praised, contains multiple historic debuts and strong jams that keep the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar tone and vocals repeatedly praised – especially on Ripple, New Speedway Boogie and during the acoustic numbers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Piano player not identified; speculation points to Howard Wales or Ned Lagin, but no direct performance praise.
